entries.title: Psalms 137:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Harps - Harps are here put for all instruments of musick.

entries.title: Psalms 137:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A song - Such songs as you used to sing in the temple of Zion.

entries.title: Psalms 137:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The Lord's - Those songs which were appointed by God to be sung only in his service.

entries.title: Psalms 137:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: If - If I do not value Jerusalem's prosperity more than all other delights.

entries.title: Psalms 137:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The day - In the time of its destruction.

entries.title: Psalms 137:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Happy - As being God's instrument to vindicate his honour, and execute his just judgments.
